name: XTREME-S
description: XTREME-S is a benchmark for evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages. It covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval. Covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families, XTREME-S aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation, as well as catalyze research in universal speech representation learning.
creator: Google Research, Hugging Face, Meta AI
citeAs: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson. XTREME-S: Evaluating Cross-lingual Speech Representations. arXiv:2203.10752v3 [cs.CL] 13 Apr 2022
rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S groups several multilingual speech datasets including Fleurs (2009 n-way parallel sentences from FLoRes dev and devtest), Multilingual LibriSpeech (derived from read audiobooks of Librivox in 8 languages), VoxPopuli (from European Parliament sessions in 23 languages), CoVoST-2 (multilingual speech translation corpus), MINDS-14 (intent classification from e-banking domain in 14 languages). For Fleurs, between one and three recordings were collected for each sentence (2.3 on average).
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Direct measurement, Software Collection, Web Scraping
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Fleurs uses sentences from the FLoRes machine translation benchmark. MLS is derived from read audiobooks of Librivox. VoxPopuli is derived from European Parliament session recordings (400k hours of unannotated speech). CoVoST-2 is a large-scale multilingual speech translation corpus. MINDS-14 is extracted from the e-banking domain. Unlabeled speech is available through MLS, VoxPopuli, CommonVoice corpora. Unlabeled text data is available through Common Crawl data as in the mC4 dataset.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For Fleurs, new train-dev-test splits were built with 1509, 150 and 350 sentences for train, dev and test respectively. Speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets. For MINDS-14, monolingual datasets were merged into a single multilingual dataset, with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split. Scripts are provided to download and easily reproduce the preprocessing steps.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For Fleurs speech recognition, transcriptions are provided. For speech translation (CoVoST-2), translations from 21 languages into English are provided. For MINDS-14, intent labels from the e-banking domain are provided covering 14 intents. For Fleurs-LangID, language labels are used. For speech retrieval, text transcriptions are used as targets.
rai:annotationsPerItem: For Fleurs, between one and three recordings for each sentence (2.3 on average)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Datasets and fine-tuning scripts are made easily accessible through the HuggingFace platform at https://hf.co/datasets/google/xtreme_s. The paper mentions that some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the Fleurs dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings). Updates will be made on the platform.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The 102 languages cover various language families and geographical locations including Western Europe/Americas, Eastern Europe, Central-Asia, Middle-East, North-Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, South-East Asia and CJK languages. Speaker information is controlled in Fleurs where speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster. The benchmark aims to support rapid development and make better speech technology available in all languages of the world.
rai:dataBiases: Results are much better on the Western European group (with 11.5 average WER) than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African (26.7 average WER) or South Asian (20.7), which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages from MLS and VoxPopuli. Reducing the gaps across geographical groups is an important research direction.
rai:dataLimitations: The tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g. speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated. Speech data is not abundant for all languages. The training sets range from a few hours to a few hundred hours of labeled data per language, representing a few-shot setting suited for low-resource understanding. On Fleurs-LangID, avoiding overfitting on speaker ID for the LangID task is essential for obtaining good performance. Speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting given the discrepancy between the richness of the input signal (speaker, domain, recording conditions) and the small number of output labels.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The benchmark is designed for evaluating cross-lingual transfer learning and multilingual speech representation learning. Tasks should be trainable with a reasonable amount of time (few days) and compute (few GPUs). The benchmark strongly encourages data-efficient self-supervised representation learning. Multilingual fine-tuning is used for most tasks. Users should detail which data they use and settings should be reproducible by the community. The benchmark encourages submissions that leverage publicly available speech and text datasets.
